description:
We are building a team for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, focusing on “Dancing with the SARs.” Our goal is to use NASA-ISRO NISAR satellite data, GIS, and AI/ML to monitor floods, land changes, wetlands, and environmental risks, starting with Patna, India. 

We welcome members interested in Python, AI/ML, GIS, Remote Sensing, Web Development, UI/UX, Data Science, and Earth Science. 

Beginners willing to learn are welcome!
summary:
BHU LOKA is a geospatial research framework developed to investigate urban flooding and compound hydro-thermal risks using Earth observation data. Demonstrated over Patna, India, the project combines Sentinel-1 SAR change analysis, NASA Terra MODIS land-surface temperature observations, Copernicus GLO-30 elevation data, and WorldPop population estimates.

Its key contribution is a dual-signal SAR approach that examines both open-water specular backscatter reduction and urban building–water double-bounce responses. This helps investigate why conventional open-water-only thresholds may overlook complex inundation patterns in dense urban environments. The framework also analyses terrain depressions, population exposure, and spatial model performance using five-fold Spatial Block Cross-Validation.

A separate synthetic simulation benchmark evaluates how spatial validation can change model performance; it is explicitly distinguished from observed satellite results. BHU LOKA aims to support more transparent, reproducible geospatial analysis for urban flood research and disaster-risk understanding.
details:
What BHU LOKA does

BHU LOKA is a dual-track geospatial research framework for analysing urban flood patterns and related environmental conditions. The current empirical study focuses on Patna Municipal Corporation, Bihar, using the September 2019 flood event as a historical case study.

1. Empirical Earth Observation Track

  • Sentinel-1A and Sentinel-1B C-band SAR GRD VV scenes from 23 and 29 September 2019 are analysed for backscatter change.
  • Two complementary radar responses are investigated: open-water specular backscatter reduction and building–water dihedral double-bounce response.
  • Copernicus GLO-30 elevation data are used to examine terrain depressions.
  • NASA Terra MODIS MOD11A1.061 observations are used to study pre-monsoon land-surface temperature.
  • WorldPop 2020 population estimates provide demographic exposure context.
  • A Random Forest classifier is evaluated using five-fold Spatial Block Cross-Validation across 60,000 aligned pixels.

2. Simulation Proxy Benchmark

A separate synthetic benchmark of 3,200 points uses Random Forest and Quantile Gradient Boosting to examine sensitivity to spatial validation and controlled hydro-thermal conditions. These outputs are simulations, not observed flood forecasts or satellite measurements.

Why it matters

Urban flooding can produce complex radar responses around buildings and dense infrastructure. A method relying only on open-water backscatter reduction may miss some urban inundation signatures. BHU LOKA investigates a complementary SAR interpretation approach and makes spatial validation, data provenance, and uncertainty important parts of the workflow.

Tools and technologies

The research workflow uses Python, geospatial raster processing, Sentinel-1 SAR, NASA MODIS, Copernicus DEM, WorldPop, scikit-learn, Random Forest, Quantile Gradient Boosting, and Spatial Block Cross-Validation.

Intended impact

The project aims to support transparent, reproducible Earth-observation research and improve understanding of urban flood mapping challenges. It is a research framework, not an operational warning service. Further independent ground validation and additional observations are required before operational use.
